coverage.method: Every image opened individually with view_image. No source, keys or other reviewer results inspected.

recognition: Recognize science-fiction RTS imagery as StarCraft-like, WWII battle imagery as Company of Heroes-like, and tactical room/market imagery as Door Kickers-like. Exact title attribution is not required for scores; recognizable identity cannot be fully blinded.

view-01.png.evidence: Bright layered blast, sparks and lighting unify dense science-fiction units and rocky terrain; the explosion partly obscures targets.
view-01.png.regressions: Bloom and unit overlap constrain readability.

view-02.png.evidence: Soft airfield view has tree clusters, apron, service boxes and distinct roof faces; player overlaps the central hangar.
view-02.png.regressions: Soft edges and cyan roof marker leave player/structure separation ambiguous.

view-03.png.evidence: Sharper hangar roof edges, directional shadows, runway markings and service yard establish several material layers.
view-03.png.regressions: Cyan roof shape is ambiguous; repeated grass and flat apron remain simple.

view-04.png.evidence: Apartment rooms have differentiated tile/wood, furniture, wall thickness and coherent light pools; paths remain readable.
view-04.png.regressions: Small figures and tactical markings compete in the hall.

view-05.png.evidence: Soft coast view separates pale plane from grass; trees cast directional shadows and rocks have several faces.
view-05.png.regressions: Coast is a uniform strip without convincing shallows; soft aircraft detail.

view-06.png.evidence: Soft crowded carrier view has orange impacts, smoke arcs and a small player ring; pale enemies separate from dark water.
view-06.png.regressions: Planes overlap player and deck; small ring does not recover the full silhouette; coarse wake.

view-07.png.evidence: Sharp airfield repeats readable runway, raised hangars, tree shadows and grouped service objects.
view-07.png.regressions: No material quality gain over the comparable sharp airfield is visible; player crosses roof geometry.

view-08.png.evidence: Quiet sharp carrier has a raised island, dark rim/hull and coherent deck markings against irregular blue water.
view-08.png.regressions: Player merges into deck; stern wake repeats soft puffs and water detail outpaces model detail.

view-09.png.evidence: Sharp coast shows aircraft highlights, faceted rocks and directional tree shadows with clear HUD.
view-09.png.regressions: Straight tan shoreline has little water transition; terrain plots remain flat.

view-10.png.evidence: Sharp sparse fight retains raised carrier silhouette, distinct orange impacts, smoke and player indicator.
view-10.png.regressions: Player still overlaps deck and hostile aircraft; dark ocean masks shadows.

view-11.png.evidence: Rain battlefield has reflective wet ground, rubble, smoke volume and luminous tracer integrating varied materials.
view-11.png.regressions: Dark soldiers and debris are hard to separate at phone scale.

view-12.png.evidence: Soft airfield presents apron, runway, hangars, service boxes and varied tree groups with coherent shading.
view-12.png.regressions: Equivalent quality to the other soft airfield; player and cyan marker overlap roof.

view-13.png.evidence: Sharp coast keeps crisp plane and rock edges, directional tree shadows and distinct land/water color families.
view-13.png.regressions: No visible meaningful improvement over the other sharp coast; thin uniform beach remains schematic.

view-14.png.evidence: Sharp quiet carrier uses a rounded rectangular tan deck with detailed stripes, dark island and attached wake.
view-14.png.regressions: Deck now appears a flat slab above a separately protruding pointed hull; perimeter depth cue is weaker than view08.

view-15.png.evidence: Marketplace has varied stalls, produce, paving, props and consistent warm shadows; routes are clearly colored.
view-15.png.regressions: Crowd density and long route overlays compete with small actors.

view-16.png.evidence: Soft quiet carrier retains clean HUD, tan markings and a visible island against dark water.
view-16.png.regressions: Rounded slab deck and exposed pointed hull appear poorly integrated; softness further weakens hull thickness versus view21.

view-17.png.evidence: Fog battlefield layers terrain, broken buildings, autumn trees, vehicles and distant haze with localized impacts.
view-17.png.regressions: Muted silhouettes and haze reduce immediate unit readability.

view-18.png.evidence: Soft sparse combat has visible orange hits and player ring with raised rim around the carrier.
view-18.png.regressions: Deck/player overlap and coarse repeated wake remain; smaller fire and smoke are soft.

view-19.png.evidence: Soft coastline retains legible plane position, grass plots, faceted rocks and shaded trees.
view-19.png.regressions: Visually equivalent to the other soft coast; uniform beach and soft model edges remain.

view-20.png.evidence: Soft sparse fight shows readable orange impacts and ring but carrier is dominated by a plain rounded slab.
view-20.png.regressions: Hull protrudes separately below deck and edge depth drops relative to view18; player overlap remains.

view-21.png.evidence: Soft quiet carrier has a clear dark hull/rim beneath tan deck and raised island, with attached stern wake.
view-21.png.regressions: Plane blends with deck markings; blurred model edges and repeated wake puffs limit polish.

view-22.png.evidence: Sharp dense fight has raised island, bright impact flecks and multiple smoke arcs amid legible pale aircraft.
view-22.png.regressions: Crowded central overlap makes player identity difficult; individual effects are small and repetitive.

view-23.png.evidence: Sharp sparse combat retains crisp plane and orange effects, deck stripes and attached wake.
view-23.png.regressions: Rounded deck reduces rim/hull integration versus view10; lower pointed hull reads as a separate shape.

view-24.png.evidence: Sharp dense combat retains differentiated bright fire and gray smoke with crisp enemy silhouettes.
view-24.png.regressions: Rounded tan deck loses strong hull edge, adding flatter geometry to an already crowded player/deck overlap.

view-25.png.evidence: Soft dense combat still shows ring, orange impact flecks and pale aircraft on dark ocean.
view-25.png.regressions: Soft flat slab carrier and protruding pointed hull reduce depth/coherence versus view06; player remains buried.

general_findings: Land/coast image pairs have no meaningful visible quality difference at this size; scores remain anchored.
Rounded rectangular carrier decks weaken visible hull integration and perimeter depth relative to the pointed rim variants. A more realistic planform alone does not establish material quality.
Dark irregular ocean supports pale-aircraft contrast but competes with subtle smoke and shadows. Clean HUD remains stronger than central combat readability.
References retain substantially richer material transitions and integrated lighting, while some have lower unit readability.
regressions: Views14/16/20/23/24/25: flat rounded deck slab with exposed pointed hull below, weaker perimeter thickness and structural integration.
The crowded views remain difficult to parse despite a small gold player indicator.
recommendations: Build a continuous visible deck edge and supporting hull beneath the rounded planform; align hull volume and deck silhouette with controlled overhang and directional shading.
Keep the player silhouette recoverable over tan deck and overlapping enemies, beyond merely locating its center.
Replace repeated wake puffs with tapered foam and irregular breakup; improve coastal shallow-water transitions.
Reduce ocean competition around subtle smoke/shadows while preserving pale plane contrast.
